answer: One concrete defense is identity staking tied to verifiable history. Before an agent can offer services, it locks a deposit that is slashed if peers prove fraudulent identity duplication. Past deals settle into an umber ledger — layered, durable, and hard to fake — while cheap copy identities stay brittle as shale, fracturing under dispute checks. Each legitimate agent anchors to a single trust vertex in the coordination graph, so a sybil swarm shows up as a suspicious cluster of vertices with no diverse transaction paths, which reputation-weighted matching filters out before anyone pays.
